title: U.S. House · Ohio's 3rd District
area: Central Ohio, including most of Columbus

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 3rd District D+21, a safely Democratic-leaning seat.

positions.summary: Her official site says she will protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act while moving toward a Medicare-For-All-Who-Want-It program.
positions.quote: I will continue to work to protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, while moving toward a "Medicare-For-All-Who-Want-It" program which would give Americans the option to access a Medicare-type system in lieu of private insurance.

positions.summary: Her official site says she supports reducing greenhouse gas emissions and minimizing reliance on fossil fuels, and supports the Paris Climate Agreement.
positions.quote: These science-backed facts are why I support taking bold steps to invest in federal programs to address climate change, prevent spending cuts to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), fully enforce the Clean Air Act, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimize our reliance on fossil fuels, and promote energy efficiency and conservation.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement on U.S. military action in Venezuela, she says military action cannot be undertaken without congressional authorization.
positions.quote: Military action cannot be undertaken without congressional authorization, clearly defined objectives, or a plan for what comes next.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served on the Committee on Financial Services in the 118th Congress (2023-2024), including as ranking member of the Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions.

candidates.name: Cleophus Dulaney

priorities.text: Campaign website lists gentrification and the affordable-housing crisis in the district as issues, citing regional projections of population growth.
Campaign website calls for a 'better relationship with our police force' and addressing homelessness and opioid-addiction rehabilitation.
Campaign website lists property taxes and home-improvement grants as an issue.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site (votedulaney.org) home and issues pages checked. The issues page lists topics only (housing, police relationship, homelessness, property taxes) without stating positions on the guide's issue statements; the home-page text on Medicare drug negotiation, tax relief and clean-energy jobs was not mapped to a guide issue. He has not completed the Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
